newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil firms rooting out bad practices-PAJ head.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil firms rooting out bad practices-PAJ head.

text.p: The chief of Japan's oil industry said on Wednesday that Japanese oil companies were slowly eliminating unfavourable business practices as they struggled to survive more than a year after market liberalisation.

Yuji Idemitsu, chairman of the Petroleum Association of Japan (PAJ), told a news conference: "Japanese oil companies have had some unfavourable business practices...which created an opaque market for Japanese consumers."
He said Japanese oil companies have had to become more cost conscious since Japan eased regulations on April 1 and they lost their virtually exclusive right to import oil products.
Liberalisation has also forced the industry to review its wholesale pricing system, he said.
Most Japanese oil companies now review their wholesale prices for oil products such as gasoline based on foreign exchange rates and crude oil price fluctuations.
Before market liberalisation, it was the practice of many Japanese oil companies to compensate petrol stations when margins between wholesale and retail prices were squeezed.
"Although it's not complete yet, I think we've had some success in (making changes)," Idemitsu said.
